findings.note: printer writes a regex literal only when the pattern also compiles as a JS RegExp, else BSONRegExp(...)
parseShellSyntaxDocument reports the error at the root node position (after leading comments)
Double/NumberDecimal/Decimal128 accept bare Infinity and NaN
lone surrogate in the error text for an unexpected astral character; position is correct, cosmetic
Date("...") without new read as a Date; recorded as an assumption
+5n accepted as NumberLong 5; harmless leniency, recorded as an assumption
\u{...} limited to 8 hex digits; larger code points are invalid anyway
positionAt counts \n, \r\n, \r as line breaks like CodeMirror-style editors; U+2028/2029 inside text are rare
regex literal choice depends on the host JS engine; BSONRegExp is always a valid fallback
